title: Paper Proposes Label-Efficient Statistical Test for Model Update Regressions
plain: A newly posted arXiv paper introduces DISCERN, a sequential two-tier statistical protocol for certifying whether a model update (retraining, fine-tuning, quantization, or vendor swap) is at least as good as the model it replaces, using mostly unlabeled traffic. angles.claim: Sign-off on a model update should require a disagreement-rate certificate, not a passed spot-check against a fixed metric threshold.
angles.audience: AI engineering leads who approve model promotions in utilities and critical infrastructure
angles.rank_reason: Directly changes what an engineer checks before promoting an update, and is exactly what the paper's zero-label tier supports.

angles.claim: Ask what fraction of promoted updates were certified with zero labels versus how many were rubber-stamped on partial manual review.
angles.audience: Directors who oversee model update governance
angles.rank_reason: Gives a concrete Thursday question a director can ask, grounded in the paper's 56% zero-label certification figure, though it acts on a single unreplicated study.

angles.claim: A vendor swap or quantization pass should be treated as a regression risk requiring a labeling budget plan, not a deployment formality.
angles.audience: AI engineering leads managing vendor model swaps and quantization pipelines
angles.rank_reason: Reframes a routine operational step as a governed decision point, weaker than the first two because it restates the paper's scope list rather than its statistical result.
